note: The transonic drag curve now peaks where the wind tunnel says it does. Three drag terms were each ramping up to a maximum at the top of their transonic bridge rather than near Mach 1.05 — on the NASA ARCAS that put a false peak at exactly Mach 1.500 and gave the drag curve two humps. Supersonic drag on finned bodies also decayed far too fast above Mach 2 (the band Western-US fliers actually use). Also new: a protuberance component, drag sweeps at altitude or on a file's Mach-Alt table, .xlsx export with live Excel charts, and charts that expand, reset and say how to pan them.
